tools.name: find_auspicious_windows
tools.description:
Find ranked auspicious time windows for an ACTIVITY on/around a date at a location.
    activity: one of meeting, sign, deal, launch, money, purchase, hiring, travel (else 'general').
    date: 'YYYY-MM-DD'. days: scan this many days from date (1 = just that day). location as lat/lon +
    IANA tz (defaults to Lucknow). Optional birth_date 'YYYY-MM-DD' (+ birth_time 'HH:MM', birth_place_tz)
    adds personal Tarabala/Chandrashtama. For activity='travel', pass direction (north/south/east/west,
    the compass direction of the journey) to apply Disha Shool + Panchaka-South rules - ask the user for
    it if they haven't said. Returns ranked, tier-graded windows with reasons;
    hard stops (Rahu Kaal, Vishti, Amavasya, Vyatipata/Vaidhriti, gandanta, eclipses) and strong
    avoids (Yamaganda, Kala, combust karakas) never surface as recommended.

activity.title: Activity

tools.name: festival_dates
tools.description:
Hindu festival calendar for a YEAR at a location - the Gregorian date each major
    festival falls on, computed from the panchang (tithi-vyapini + sankranti), not scraped.
    Covers Diwali, Holi-season, Navratri, Janmashtami, Ganesh Chaturthi, Maha Shivaratri,
    Ram Navami, Akshaya Tritiya, Vijayadashami/Dussehra, Guru Purnima, Nag/Vasant Panchami,
    Hanuman Jayanti, and the Sankrantis. location as lat/lon + IANA tz (defaults to Lucknow).
    Janmashtami uses the full nisitha + Rohini/Jayanti determination; janmashtami_school
    selects the reckoning: 'madhava' (default, mainstream - Jayanti shifts to the Rohini day)
    or 'hemadri' (keep the midnight date). ekadashi_sampradaya selects the ekadashi reckoning:
    'vaishnava' (default, mainstream/udaya - the later day every published panchang shows) or
    'smarta' (grihastha - the earlier day in a vrddhi year). Regional note: a few festivals
    (ekadashi smarta/vaishnava split, Holika bhadra, some sankrantis) can differ by a day by
    tradition/region - relay the computed date, note it may vary locally.

tools.name: explain_recommendation
tools.description:
Explain WHY a specific moment is (or isn't) auspicious - factor by factor, in plain language.
    Use this when the user asks 'why did you suggest that time?', 'why is Rahu Kaal bad?', or wants to
    understand the reasoning, not just the verdict. Teaches each factor (what it is + why the tradition
    weighs it) and shows the raw scoring. To compare two times, call this twice and contrast the results.
    datetime_local: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' in the location's local time. Same location/birth/direction
    params as check_time (direction: travel's compass heading, for Disha Shool teaching).

tools.name: get_choghadiya_schedule
tools.description:
Dense: the choghadiya schedule for a date+location - the eight parts of the daytime, each
    with its name and whether it is favourable. Choghadiya is the FIRST thing many readers in
    Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan look at, and it had no tool of its own while the hora did.
    Two things this carries that a bare good/avoid list cannot: it is reckoned for the DAY only
    (there is no night table), and where a normally-favourable slot is marked avoid it names the
    kaala that took those minutes, because the sourced kaala outranks the almanac label.

tools.name: get_next_eclipse
tools.description:
Upcoming eclipses (grahana) for a location, soonest first. For each: date, kind (solar/lunar)
    + type (Total/Partial/Annular), the nakshatra it falls in, and whether it is VISIBLE from this
    place. Muhurta meaning: where an eclipse is visible, its hours AND the sutak before them (about
    12h solar / 9h lunar) are a hard block - no new work, the time given to japa/dana/snana; visible
    or not, the days bracketing it (a few each side, more for solar) and its nakshatra stay unsettled
    for major beginnings. Answers 'when is the next eclipse?' / 'surya grahan kab hai?'.
